idiom_name: class methods as named constructors (Date.parse, File.open) plus Kernel conversion functions
implementation_notes: Class#new is itself an ordinary method (allocate plus initialize), so naming a creation route is just defining another class method: Date.parse, File.open (which yields the object and closes it deterministically), Struct.new and the Kernel conversion functions Integer(), Float(), Hash() and String() are the standard-library examples. The classic structure becomes `private_class_method :new` plus `def self.from_x`, which is rarely necessary because Ruby's conversion functions already own the parse-and-validate role; keep it when every construction must go through a validating route, and use a block-taking creator whenever the object owns a resource that must be released.
pitfalls: private_class_method :new does not stop allocate, dup or Marshal.load, so the invariant only holds for ordinary callers - serialization and reflection construct objects directly.
A creator that returns a cached object exposes mutable state to every caller; freeze shared instances or return copies.
Hard-coding the class name inside the creator (Temperature.new instead of an implicit-receiver new) breaks subclassing and code reloading silently; call new on self so subclasses inherit the routes.
